en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washha who said, ‘Abdul Kareem Bin Amro narrated to me, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>: ‘The one who dies and there isn’t an Imam<sup>asws</sup> for him, so his death would be a death of the ignorance (Pre-Islamic period)’,
I said, ‘A death of disbelief?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Death of straying’.
I said, ‘So the one who dies today, and there isn’t an Imam<sup>asws</sup> for him, so his death would be a death of the ignorance (Pre-Islamic period)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ who has said that ‘Abd al-Karim ibn ‘Amr narrated to me from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following.
“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words the Messenger of Allah. ““Whoever would die and is not under the (guardianship) of the Imam his death would be like a death in ignorance.”
The narrator has said I then asked, “Is it death in disbelief (in religion)?” He said, “It is death in error .”
I then said, “Thus, whoever would die today and would not have an Imam would his death be considered as if he has died in ignorance (without religion)?” He said, “Yes, that is true.”
